rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says Pharaoh's upbringing was only outwardly a favor; in truth Pharaoh's subjugation of Israel and killing its sons caused Moses to be brought up in Pharaoh's house.
rows.anchor: تعبيدك بني إسرائيل وقصدك إياهم بذبح أبنائهم فإن السبب في وقوعى عندك وحصولى في تربيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Pharaoh not oppressed Israel and killed its sons, Moses's mother would have raised him instead of casting him into the river; Pharaoh cannot claim credit for the result of his own abuse.
rows.anchor: لو لم يفعل فرعون ذلك أي قهر بني إسرائيل وذبح أبنائهم لتكفلت أم موسى بتربيته ولما قذفته في اليم حتى يصل إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, تلك is the subject, نعمة its predicate, تمنها علي an adjective, and أن عبدت the predicate of an omitted subject meaning Pharaoh's enslavement of Moses's people.
rows.anchor: قوله تلك مبتدأ ونعمة خبرها وتمنها علي صفة وإن عبدت خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي وهي في الحقيقة تعبيد قومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term taʿbīd means taking someone as a slave, overpowering and humiliating him; Bursevī also gives a Persian gloss for it.
rows.anchor: والتعبيد : بالفارسية (دام كردن وببند كي كرفتن) يقال عبدته إذا أخذته عبدا وقهرته وذللته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses first answered Pharaoh's reproach as an attack on his prophethood, then addressed the alleged favor without denying its factual truth and showed its real consequence was a favor.
rows.anchor: رد موسى عليه السلام أولا ما وبخه فرعون قدحا في نبوته ثم رجع إلى ما عده عليه من النعمة ولم يصرح برده حيث كان صدقا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One commentator says Pharaoh began like a vulgar commoner by recalling that he had fed and favored God's prophet; mannah is a weighty favor.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : بدأ فرعون بكلام السفلة ومن على نبي الله بما أطعمه والمنة النعمة الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mannah can mean an actual deed of favor; properly, only God truly does this, as in the verse about God favoring believers.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون ذلك بالفعل فيقال : من فلان على فلان إذا أثقله بالنعمة وعلى ذلك قوله تعالى : {لقد من الله على المؤمنين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mannah can also mean verbally recounting a favor, normally reprehensible except when answering ingratitude; sayings warn that such reminders destroy good deeds but can expose ungratefulness.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون ذلك بالقول وذلك مستقبح فيما بين الناس إلا عند كفران النعمة ولقبح ذلك قيل : المنة تهدم الصنيعة

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī says spiritual chivalry does not consist in recalling favors to those one has helped; Pharaoh showed his lack of chivalry by doing so to Moses.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي قدس سره : ليس من الفتوة تذكار الصنائع وتعدادها على من اصطنعت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans can manifest divine gentleness in a way angels cannot, which is why the angels prostrated to humanity.
rows.anchor: ليعلم أن للإنسان استعدادا في إظهار صفة اللطف لم يكن للملك ولذلك صار الإنسان مسجودا للملك والملك ساجده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: This Sufi reading makes Moses a manifestation of divine gentleness and Pharaoh a manifestation of overpowering wrath; prophetic hardship brings both to the fullness of their contrasting dispositions, a pattern repeated in every age.
rows.anchor: كذا في "التأويلات النجمية" وقس عليهما كل موسى وكل فرعون في كل عصر إلى قيام الساعة فإن الأشياء تتبين بالأضداد وتبلغ إلى كمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is an interrogative meaning 'what'; rabb means the one who nurtures and manages creatures' welfare, and the worlds are all besides God. Pharaoh asks the supposed messenger about the Lord's essence and kind, denying any lord beyond himself.
rows.anchor: ما استفهامية معناها أي شيء والرب المربي والمتكفل لمصلحة الموجودات والعالم اسم لما سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says Pharaoh had heard Moses claim to be a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and arrogantly asked what the Lord of the worlds was as a test of His essence.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون فرعون شنيده بودكه موسى كفت أنا رسول رب العالمين أسلوب سخن كبر دانيد وازروي امتحان كفت يست روردكار عالميان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God's essence cannot be defined as a composite of genus and difference, Moses answers by describing God through external relations and attributes.
rows.anchor: ولما لم يمكن تعريفه تعالى إلا بلوازمه الخارجية لاستحالة التركيب في ذاته من جنس وفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens and earth repeats the meaning of Lord of the worlds and prevents Pharaoh from narrowing the claim to his own kingdom.
rows.anchor: عين ما أراده بالعالمين لئلا يحمله اللعين على ما تحت مملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those certain through sound reasoning know that the world comprises creation from which its maker is known, and that its Lord created, provides for, and governs it; this is the answer to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: {إن كنتم موقنين} بالأشياء المحققين لها بالنظر الصحيح الذي يؤدي إلى الإتيان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says no one can know God's reality: whatever intellect, understanding, imagination, senses, or analogy can contain is created and cannot encompass the Creator.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (هي كس را از حقيقة حق آكاهي ممكن نيست هره در عقل وفهم ووهم وحواس وقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God means knowing Him through His relation to creation and the world's emanation from Him within human capacity; perfect knowers are bewildered by what exceeds that capacity and admit their inability to know Him fully.
rows.anchor: فمعنى العلم بالله العلم به من حيث الارتباط بينه وبين الخلق وانتشار العالم منه بقدر الطاقة البشرية إذ منه ما لا توفيه الطاقة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh addresses the people around him because he fears Moses's answer will affect their hearts and make them follow Moses.
rows.anchor: {قال} فرعون عند سماع جوابه خوفا من تأثيره في قلوب قومه وانقيادهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those around Pharaoh are the Egyptian Coptic nobles; the word حول refers to the side of an object toward which one can turn.
rows.anchor: {لمن حوله} من أشراف قومه وهم القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His question 'Do you not listen?' tells them to hear and marvel at Moses's words, while insinuating Pharaoh's own lordship.
rows.anchor: {ألا تستمعون} ما يقول فاستمعوه وتعجبوا منه في مقاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses clarifies further by demoting Pharaoh from lordship to the status of one ruled, calling God the Lord of Pharaoh and his earliest ancestors.
rows.anchor: {قال} موسى زيادة في البيان وحطا له عن مرتبة الربوبية إلى مرتبة المربوبية

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says Moses moved from the apparent signs to signs nearer and clearer to the observer.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (عدول كرد از ظهر آيات باقرب آيات بناظر وواضح آن بر متأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Pharaoh claimed lordship over people of his own era but not earlier generations, so Moses showed the true Lord rules every age.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن فرعون كان يدعي الربوبية على أهل عصره وزمانه فلم يدع ذلك على من كان قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī says Pharaoh's next words arise from foolishness and an effort to turn his people away from accepting the truth.
rows.anchor: {قال} فرعون من سفاهته وصرفا لقومه عن قبول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh sarcastically calls Moses 'your messenger' and says his words cannot come from a rational person; he addresses the others to avoid implying Moses was also sent to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: لا يصدر ما قاله عن العقلاء وسماه رسولا على السخرية وإضافة إلى مخاطبيه ترفعا من أن يكون مرسلا إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon defines madness as a barrier between the soul and intellect.
rows.anchor: والجنون حائل بين النفس والعقل كما في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses continues defining the truth and does not engage Pharaoh's foolish insult.
rows.anchor: {قال} موسى زيادة في تعريف الحق ولم يشتغل بمجاوبته في السفاهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning East and West explicitly clarifies God's rule over the heavens, earth, and all between them, including recurring changes from light to darkness that require a wise, knowing originator.
rows.anchor: أراد التصريح بذكر الشروق والغروب للتغيرات الحادثة في العالم من النور مرة والظلمة أخرى المفتقرة إلى محدث عليم حكيم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the verse inwardly: God lights His friends' hearts with faith and their exteriors, while darkening enemies' hearts with disbelief and showing darkness on their bodies.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : 269 منور قلوب أوليائه بالإيمان ومشرق ظواهرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Pharaoh's audience had reason or discernment, they would recognize Moses's claim and infer the cause from its effect.
rows.anchor: {إن كنتم تعقلون} شيئا من الأشياء أو من جملة من له عقل وتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse hints that Pharaoh's people lack reason and bear the very madness they accuse Moses of; opposing temperaments, like Moses and Pharaoh or heart and lower soul, each call the other's state madness.
rows.anchor: وفيه تلويح بأنهم بمعزل من دائرة العقل متصفون بما رموه عليه السلام به من الجنون فمن كمال ضدية موسى وفرعون وكذا القلب والنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same contrast applies to lover and ascetic: the madness of love and the madness of renunciation belong to different realms.
rows.anchor: وقس عليهما العاشق والزاهد فإن جنون العشق من واد وجنون الزهد من واد آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After losing the argument, Pharaoh abandons debate for a tyrant's threat, driven by rebellion, anger that lordship was attributed elsewhere, and perhaps a materialist belief that ruling a region by power merits worship.
rows.anchor: {قال} فرعون من غاية تمرده وميلا إلى العقوبة كما يفعله الجبابرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One commentator says Pharaoh was an anthropomorphist and asked what the Lord of the worlds was in order to imagine Him.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كان الملعون مشبها ولذلك قال وما رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These stories console the Prophet, whose radiant heart grieved at his people's denial despite the miracles; they teach him to emulate earlier prophets' patience and await relief.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تسلية للنبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: A poem attributed to al-Ḥāfiẓ promises glad tidings from the unseen: one will not remain forever at the world's door.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : سروش عالم غيبم بشارتي خوش داد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تلاوة means reading in connected succession, while qirāʾa is broader; the command tells Muhammad to recite to Arab polytheists and inform Meccans.
rows.anchor: {واتل عليهم} من التلاوة وهي القراءة على سبيل التتابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Abraham is a report of great importance.
rows.anchor: {نبأ إبراهيم} خبره العظيم الشان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the Meccans properly claimed descent from Abraham, took pride in being his descendants, and relied on that lineage.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (خبر إبراهيم كه إيشان بدو نسبت درست ميكنند وبفرزندي أو مفخترند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'when he said' is a temporal adverb linked to 'report'; Abraham's father is Āzar, as discussed earlier, and his people are the inhabitants of Babylon in Iraq, a place associated with sorcery.
rows.anchor: {إذ قال} ظرف لنبأ {لأبيه} آزر وهو تاريخ كما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawm originally denotes men rather than women, as in the verse about men being maintainers of women, though Qur'anic usage often includes women too.
rows.anchor: والقوم جماعة الرجال في الأصل دون النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham already knew his people worshipped idols; he asked what they worship to alert them to their error and show that their objects did not deserve worship.
rows.anchor: سألهم وقد علم أنهم عبدة الأوثان لينبههم على ضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفرأيتم asks whether they looked and saw, or reflected and understood; the question challenges what they and their earliest ancestors worshipped, since age and longstanding practice cannot make falsehood true.
rows.anchor: {أفرءيتم} أي : أنظرتم فأبصرتم أو تأملتم فعلمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham explains that the idols harm their worshippers more than a person is harmed by an enemy; calling lifeless idols enemies is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: {فإنهم عدو لى} بيان لحال ما يعبدونه بعد التنبيه على عدم علمهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying the idols are enemies to himself rather than explicitly to his listeners, Abraham advises them more tactfully and models advice by beginning with himself.
rows.anchor: لا لكم تعريضا لهم فإنه أنفع في النصح من التصريح

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the wording as inversion: it means 'I am their enemy,' since one who takes someone as an enemy is opposed in return; عدو is singular as a verbal noun or relational adjective.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : هو من المقلوب ومعناه فإني عدو لهم فإن من عاديته عاداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا رب العالمين is a disconnected exception: the Lord is unlike the idols and is Abraham's friend in this life and the next, continually granting benefits.
rows.anchor: {إلا رب العالمين} استثناء منقطع أي لكن رب العالمين ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: One of the great Sufi masters says Abraham viewed himself as uniquely God's intimate friend, beyond comparison in his age, and so experienced enmity with all creation.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : رأى الخليل عليه السلام نفسه بمثابة في الخلة لم يكن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This also reports Abraham's perfect love: no one but the Real is worthy of companionship and love.
rows.anchor: وأيضا هذا إخبار عن كمال محبته إذ لا يليق بصحبته ومحبته أحد غيرالحق

rows.speaker: سمنون
rows.claim: Samnūn says love is not sound until one looks on the worlds with enmity, thereby loving the Beloved and returning to Him through detachment from all else.
rows.anchor: قال سمنون : لا تصح المحبة لمن لم ينظر إلى الأكوان وما فيها بعين العداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says an enemy is not looked at, or is viewed only askance for lack of affection; a traveler toward God should regard other-than-God only contemplatively.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن العدو لا ينظر إلى العدو إلا بطرف العين بل لا ينظر أصلا لفقدان الميل القلبي قطعا فإذا كان ما سوى الله تعالى عدوا للسائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two eyes signify the spiritual and physical realms: while the left eye attends to the physical kingdom, the right eye is veiled from the spiritual kingdom, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: وقد ركب الله في الإنسان عينين إشارة باليمنى إلى الملكوت وباليسرى إلى الملك فما دامت اليسرى مفتوحة إلى الملك فاليمنى محجوبة عن الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker must withdraw attention from both the physical and spiritual realms and direct it to the divine omnipotence and supreme realm; this is approved blindness and vision.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من قطع النظر عن الملك والملكوت وإيصاله إلى عام الجبروت واللاهوت وهو العمى المقبول والنظر المرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer asks God to occupy the worshippers with Him and turn them away from everything besides Him.
rows.anchor: وفي الدعاء : اللهم اشغلنا بك عمن سواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although all creation is an effect of divine theophany, it is an enemy as an idol or source of attachment; crossing all levels and seeing God in everything dissolves otherness.
rows.anchor: قلت : هو في نفسه كذلك لكنه إشارة إلى المراتب ولا بد من العبور عن جميع المراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes that for the one who sees God in every thing, each former enemy becomes a friend, and the world is a mirror of the Beloved's beauty.
rows.anchor: فمن شاهد الله في كل شيء فقد انقطع عن الأغيار فكل عدو له صديق والحمد تعالى : جهان مر آت حسن شاهد ماست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'who created me' describes the Lord of the worlds, who brought Abraham from nonbeing into being.
rows.anchor: {الذى خلقنى} (از عدم بوجود آورد) صفة رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone guides Abraham to the welfare of both abodes through guidance beginning with creation and the continuing gift of spirit; the fāʾ and present tense indicate its ongoing renewal.
rows.anchor: {فهو} وحده {يهدين} يرشدني إلى صلاح الدارين بهدايته المتصلة من الخلق ونفخ الروح متجدد على الاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance begins with the fetus being directed to absorb blood in the womb and culminates in guidance to the path of Paradise and its delights.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن مبدأ الهداية بالنسبة إلى الإنسان هداية الجنين إلى امتصاص دم الحيض من الرحم ومنتهاها الهداية إلى طريق الجنة والتنعم بلذائذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording points to abandoning reliance on causes and acquisition in prophethood, sainthood, and intimacy with God: these are gifts rooted in primordial election, though their gradual appearance can mislead the veiled into thinking they were earned.
rows.anchor: بل أشار إلى الاصطفاء الأزلي وذلك أن جميع المقامات اختصاصية عطائية غير نسبية حاصلة للعين الثابتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's cited couplet contrasts people who strive for union with those who entrust it to fixed divine decree.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : قومي بجهد وجد نهادند وصل دوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated relative pronoun in three clauses shows that each divine attribute independently establishes the Lord's claim.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الموصول في المواقع الثلاثة للدلالة على أن كل واحدة من الصلات مستقلة باقتضاء الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone feeds Abraham whatever food He wills and gives him whatever drink He wills.
rows.anchor: {هو} وحده {يطعمنى} أي طعام شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding and giving drink include more than creating and handing over food: God also grants appetite, chewing, swallowing, digestion, and elimination, all needed to benefit from them.
rows.anchor: وليس الإطعام والسقي عبارتين عن مجرد خلق الطعام والشراب له

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra's prayer asks God for a grinding molar, a digesting stomach, and an effective bowel, underscoring the bodily means required to benefit from food.
rows.anchor: ومن دعاء أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه : "اللهم اجعل لي ضرسا طحونا ومعدة هضوما ودبرا بثورا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to trust, contentment, submission, entrusting affairs to God, cutting off reliance on causes, turning fully to Him, and turning away from everything else.
rows.anchor: وأشارت الآية إلى مقام التوكل والرضى والتسليم والتفويض وقطع الأسباب والإقبال إليه بالكلية والإعراض عما سواه

rows.speaker: صاحب بحر الحقائق
rows.claim: The author of Baḥr al-Ḥaqāʾiq reads the food as worship that revives hearts and the drink as a holy manifestation of divine lordship that refreshes spirits.
rows.anchor: صاحب "بحر الحقائق" : (فرمودكه مراد طعام عبوديستت كه دلها بآن زنده شود وشراب طهور تجلى صفت ربوبيت

rows.speaker: ذو النون مصري
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī says the food is knowledge of God and the drink is love.
rows.anchor: وذو النون مصري قدس سره فرمودكه اين طعام طعام معرفتست واين شراب شراب محبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited couplet praises love's wine as the best wine and calls every other drink a mirage.
rows.anchor: شراب المحبة خير الشراب وكل شراب سواه سراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī says the prophetic report 'I spend the night with my Lord; He feeds and gives me drink' can be understood from the verse's deeper implication.
rows.anchor: واز فحواي كلام شمه از أسرار كلام حقائق نظام (أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني)

rows.speaker: أحد القولين
rows.claim: One of two reported opinions takes the prophetic feeding and drinking literally as food and drink for the mouth, noting that this reading preserves the ordinary sense of the words.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه طعام وشراب حسي للفم قالوا

rows.speaker: القول الثاني
rows.claim: The other opinion understands the prophetic nourishment as divine knowledge, intimate conversation, nearness, love, and other states that feed hearts and spirits.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد به ما يغذيه الله به من معارفه وما يفيض على قلبه من لذة مناجاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says God alone heals, correcting people who attributed illness to time and food and cure to doctors and medicines; both sickness and healing are from God, but he attributes illness to himself as proper etiquette.
rows.anchor: {فهو} وحده {يشفين} يبرئني من المرض ويعطي الشفاء لا الأطباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī compares Abraham's wording with Khidr attributing the boat's defect to himself and the boys' good outcome to God, and the jinn leaving an evil's source unnamed while attributing guidance to God.
rows.anchor: كما قال الخضر عليه السلام في العيب : {فأردت أن أعيبها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The healing clause is joined to feeding and drinking because health and illness often follow eating: overeating brings sickness, while restraint is a basis of comfort and safety.
rows.anchor: قوله : {وإذا مرضت} إلخ عطف على يطعمني ويسقيني نظمهما

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages say many of the dead would blame indigestion for their lifespans, and that a little hunger is the best thing for the stomach.
rows.anchor: قالت الحكماء : لو قيل لأكثر الموتى.

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī transmits from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq that when he becomes ill, God heals his sin through repentance.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (از امام جعفر صادق رضي الله عنه منقولست كه ون بيمار شوم بكناه مرا شفادهد بتوبه

rows.speaker: سلمى
rows.claim: Salmī reads illness as seeing otherness and healing as witnessing the lights of the One, the Overpowering.
rows.anchor: سلمى رحمه الله فرمودكه مرض برؤيت اغياراست وشفا بمشاهده أنوار واحد قهار

rows.speaker: بحر الحقائق
rows.claim: Baḥr al-Ḥaqāʾiq reads illness as attachment to the two created worlds and healing as cutting attachment through a divine attraction that joins the seeker to the One.
rows.anchor: ودربحر آورده كه بيماري بتعلقات كونين است وشفا بقطع تعلق وآن وابسته بجذبه عنا يتست

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another Sufi reading treats illness as love and longing for union with God, and healing as the beauty of His presence and unveiling.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وإذا مرضت بداء محبته وسقمت بسقم الشوق إلى لقائه ووصلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to giving up recourse to anything besides God and relying on treatment or medicine, as the perfection of surrender.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى رفع الرجوع إلى غيره والسكون إلى التداوي والمعالجة بشيء فهو كمال التسليم

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says Abraham's illness was not known at the time but was a kind of feigning illness, like scholars who pretend to be sick to receive visitors.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (وأين نه مرضى معلوم بود در آن وقت بلكه نوعي بود از تمارض) كما يتمارض الأحبار طمعا في العيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart-healing alluded to here is Gabriel's occasional visit, commissioned by God to ask Abraham how he was; Abraham's inward answer rejoices that Gabriel asked.
rows.anchor: (آن شفاي ذدل خليل كه بوي أشارت ميكند آنست كه جبريل كاه كاه آمدي بفرمان حق وكفتي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A sick, pale man who was urged to call a doctor replied that the doctor had made him ill, expressing reliance on God as the source of sickness.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه مرض وضعف اصفر لونه فقيل له ألا ندعو لك طبيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death at life's end and then raises people in the afterlife to repay their deeds; ثم marks the long interval between worldly death and resurrection.
rows.anchor: {والذى يميتنى} في الدنيا عند انقضاء الأجل {ثم يحيين} في الآخرة لمجازاة العمل أدخل ثم ههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is attributed to God as a true divine favor because it can lead perfected people to eternal life and free them from trials and suffering.
rows.anchor: ونسبة الإماتة إلى الله تعالى لأنها من النعم الإلهية في الحقيقة حيث أن الموت وصلة لأهل الكمال إلى الحياة الأبدية والخلاص من أنواع المحن والبلية

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī gives inward pairings: God kills by justice and revives by grace, or kills through sin, ignorance, greed, or separation and revives through obedience, intellect, piety, or union.
rows.anchor: أمام ثعلبي (كفته بميراند بعدل وزنده كند بفضل وكفته اندكه أماتت بمعصيت است واحيا بطاعت يا أماتت بجهل است واحيا بعقل

rows.speaker: سلمى
rows.claim: Salmi's Ḥaqāʾiq reading says God kills the self's ego and gives it life through divine guidance, which is true life.
rows.anchor: در حقايق سلمى آورده كه بميراند از سمات روحانيت وزنده كرداند بصفا تربانيت

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says one need not grieve when God is one's joy or fear when He is one's life, and need not attach the heart to the next world when God is one's present life.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : غم كي خورد رنكه شادمانيش تويي باكي برد آنكه زندكانيش تويي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks with hope rather than certainty to model proper humility, keep servants between fear and hope, and signal God's generosity, since a generous Lord fulfills hopeful expectation.
rows.anchor: دعا بلفظ الطمع ولم يعزم في سؤاله كما عزم فيما قبل من الأمور المذكورة تأدبا أو ليعلم أن العبد ليس له أن يحكم لنفسه بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham attributes the error to himself to humble himself and teach the community to avoid sin, remain wary, and seek pardon for past or possible minor sins; even the righteous's good deeds count as shortcomings for the near ones.
rows.anchor: وأسند الخطيئة إلى نفسه وهي في الغالب ما يقصد بالعرض لأنه من الخطأ هضما لنفسه وتعليما للأمة أن يجتنبوا المعاصي ويكونوا على حذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means that no one's wealth will help on Resurrection Day, even if spent on good works, and no one's sons will help, even if righteous and capable of intercession.
rows.anchor: بدل من يوم يبعثون ومفعول الفعل محذوف والتقدير لا ينفع مال أحدا وإن كان مصروفا في الدنيا إلى وجوه البر والخيرات ولا ينفع بنون فردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means that only a sincere person with a heart sound from disbelief and hypocrisy benefits; faith is required for either wealth or children to help.
rows.anchor: {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} بدل من مفعوله المحذوف أي إلا مخلصا سليم القلب

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says a sound heart is safe from disbelief and sins; the heart is named because the limbs follow its health or corruption, as in the report about the heart being a morsel of flesh.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : بنفس سليمة من الكفر والمعاصي وإنما أضافه إلى القلب لأن الجوارح

rows.speaker: ليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says disbelievers boasted of wealth and children, but these cannot help without sound hearts; Muslims benefit from good deeds and from righteous children, whether the child dies first or later prays for the parent.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : كان الكفار يقولون : نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الحكيم
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥakīm lists three signs of a sound heart: harming no one, not nursing hurt from anyone, and expecting no repayment for kindness; these show piety, loyalty, and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وسئل أبو القاسم الحكيم عن القلب السليم فقال : له ثلاث علامات أولاها : أن لا يؤذي أحدا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī reports that soundness is sincerity in the testimony of faith; he also says a sound heart is free of worldly love, while others say it is free of envy and betrayal.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (كفته اند سلامت قلب إخلاص است

rows.speaker: تيسير
rows.claim: A reading in Taysīr defines the sound heart as free from hatred of the Prophet's family, wives, and Companions.
rows.anchor: ودرتيسير كويد از بغض أهل بيت وازواج وأصحاب حضرت يغمبر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says a sound heart is empty of all besides God, worldly greed, and hope for the afterlife; another reported reading says it is free of innovation and settled upon the Sunnah.
rows.anchor: إمام قشيري رحمه الله فرمودكه قلب سليم آنست كه خالي باشد ازغير خداي ازطمع دنيا ورجاء عقبى يا خالي باشد از بدعت ومطمن بسنت

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says salīm means bitten by a snake; one bitten remains anxious and agitated, suggesting the sound heart's constant fear of separation or longing for union.
rows.anchor: واز سيد ذطائفة جنيد قدس سره منقولست كه سليم ماركزيده بود وماركزيده يوسته درقلق واضطرابست س بيان ميكند كه دل سليم مدام درمقام جزع وتضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetry describes the pain of nearness as greater than distance, with closeness bringing fear of loss and distance offering hope of reunion.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي : محنت قرب ز بعد افزونست جكر از محنت مرهم خونست

rows.speaker: بحر
rows.claim: Baḥr reads the day when wealth and children do not help as the approach to the divine presence for acceptance of God's grace.
rows.anchor: وفي "البحر" : {يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون} للوصول إلى الحضرة لقبول الفيض الإلهي

rows.speaker: بحر
rows.claim: Baḥr reads coming to God as arrival at the moment of watchfulness, with a sound heart free of the original distortion of created nature; the heart was created as a mirror for divine attributes before worldly attachments tarnished it.
rows.anchor: {إلا من أتى الله} عند المراقبة

rows.speaker: بحر
rows.claim: Baḥr says the exception points to taking on God's character and attributes: the heart is sound when it embodies sacred purity rather than looking toward creation.
rows.anchor: أشار بقوله : {إلا من} إلى التخلق بخلق الله والاتصاف بصفته

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ defines the sound heart as one untroubled by any affliction of the created world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : السليم الذي لا يشوشه شيء من آفات الكون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One person says serenity of the breast comes from observing the limits of certainty and abandoning personal will amid changing or established states.
rows.anchor: وسئل بعضهم : بم تنال سلامة الصدر؟ قال : بالوقوف على حد اليقين

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abū Yazīd recounts traveling through deserts, the spiritual world, and the angelic realm; offered all he had seen, he asked instead to want nothing, and was granted that state.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : فقطعت المفاوز حتى بلغت البوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ب in 'go with my letter' is causative; Solomon chose the hoopoe over powerful jinn because he saw signs of knowledge, wisdom, and sound judgment in it, leaving the queen no excuse.
rows.anchor: فتكون الباء للتعدية وتخصيصه بالرسالة دون سائر ما تحت ملكه من أبناء الجن الأقوياء على التصرف والتعرف لما عاين فيه من علامات العلم والحكمة وصحة الفراسة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says the hoopoe was truthful in its report, sincere in counsel to its king, and attentive to the truth, so it was rewarded with the message despite its weak outward form.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أنه لما صدق فيما أخبر وبذل النصح لملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter is to Bilqīs and her people, since the earlier wording mentions her and her people.
rows.anchor: {فألقه إليهم} أي : اطرحه على بلقيس وقومها لأنه ذكرهم معها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād explains the plural pronoun because the noble letter's message calls everyone to Islam.
rows.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : وجمع الضمير لما أن مضمون الكتاب الكريم دعوة الكل إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command ألقه with a silent hā is a valid pronunciation easing or a pause form; its underlying form has the object pronoun referring to the letter and is jussive for that reason.
rows.anchor: قوله : ألقه بسكون الهاء تخفيفا لغة صحيحة أو على نية الوقف
